newsitem.title: UK: Tesco to fly food to beat Spanish blockade.
newsitem.headline: Tesco to fly food to beat Spanish blockade.

text.p: Supermarket chain Tesco Plc is preparing to beat the Spanish lorry blockade by flying food into Britain.
"Already, moves are under way to mount a series of flights similar to those used to beat the French lorry blockade in November," Tesco said.

No flights have yet taken place but Tesco fresh produce buyer Elliott Weider said: "The infrastructure we established during the French operation is still in place. We are watching the situation closely and are quite prepared to act in our customers' interests."
Tesco was currently talking to its suppliers to decide what options were available, said spokesman Alan McLaughlin.
It was also considering using specially chartered cargo ferries from Gibraltar to keep Britain supplied with Spanish fruit and vegetables.

British Freight Transport Association (FTA) spokesman Adam Worth said: "The situation appears to be deteriorating. It started as a wildcat strike with lorries held up for a couple of hours but has been worsening with some delays reaching 12 to 16 hours but (lorries) still getting through.
"Perishables are not really held up so far but if it escalates and all major routes are blocked, it will cause real trouble.
"There are threats by the Spanish hauliers' association ASTIC that they will today (Thursday) introduce a more general blockade and we are very worried by this," Worth added.
McLaughlin said Tesco had beaten the French truckers in November blockade by flying fresh fruit and vegetables to London Gatwick in the belly holds of passenger aircraft.
Officials at rival chains J Sainsbury and ASDA said the Spainish blockade was so far not having an impact on their supplies but that they were keeping the situation under review.
In November Sainsbury chartered air freighters to fly Spanish fruit into England.
The FTA is advising its members that areas to be avoided are around Hendaye/Irun; Badajos province, the road to Portugal, from Zaragossa to Madrid and Bilbao port.
"We're asking ASTIC to calm the situation. Spanish truckers are happy to use the same tactics they criticised in France," FTA's Worth said.

In a statement Tesco said almost 25 percent of the fresh fruit and vegetables on sale in British supermarkets came from Spain at this time of year. Products affected included broccoli, celery, tomatoes, peppers and strawberries.
Spanish truckers are pushing for restructuring of their sector including retirement at 60 years instead of 65 and renegotiation of gasoline costs.
